turns.content: A one-dimensional finite well has U(x)=0 for 0<x<a and U(x)=V outside the well. A bound particle has E<V. Are the exterior regions x<0 and x>a classically allowed or forbidden?

If the exterior regions are classically forbidden for the stated state, write their general stationary Schrodinger solutions and define the corresponding decay parameter in terms of m, V, E, and hbar.
For that forbidden-region case, apply normalizability to select the physical exterior wavefunction in each region, leaving arbitrary amplitude constants.
For each conditionally selected wavefunction, separate any constant complex phase from its x-dependent factor. Does the spatial dependence carry a varying phase?
Under the same forbidden-region condition, what is the spatial phase gradient in each exterior region?
Choose a direct expression for probability current that uses the conditional exterior wavefunctions or their phase behavior.
For the case in which those exterior solutions apply, evaluate J=(hbar/(2mi))(Psi* grad Psi-Psi grad Psi*) in both regions.
For any bound-state case in which those exterior solutions apply, interpret the resulting currents physically.
Within that case, can a constant complex phase in an exterior amplitude create a nonzero spatial flux? Explain.
Conditioned on the exterior regions being forbidden, report their probability currents and the decisive wavefunction argument.
